In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
perfect prediction and causal interpolation are possible only for signals with a finite number of degrees of freedom.

perfect prediction is always possible if the sampling mechanism is a unitary operator, whereas perfect prediction is impossible for nonunitary sampling mechanisms if the spectrum of the signal has nontrivial intersection with the spectrum of the unitary sampling mechanism's inverse.
, for any deterministic signal, the causal processing of its samples is stable if and only if its samples are generated by a sampling mechanism satisfying the conditions of perfect prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the stability and predictability of the sampling mechanism, and its relationship to the signal's smoothness, are crucial in the design of stable and efficient sampling mechanisms.
we show how to perform stable causal prediction and interpolation for a wide range of deterministic signals, including those encountered in practice.
, in many situations, causal processing of the generalized samples is feasible and can be done with high precision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prediction and causal interpolation problems for a given signal are closely related.
the causal processing of a signal can always be performed in a bounded stable way if and only if the sampling mechanism has a bounded stable inverse.
causal extrapolation and interpolation of deterministic signals is feasible under very general conditions.
